subject: Economics
central_question: How did India use planning, agricultural reform, industrial policy and trade protection to pursue growth, self-reliance, modernisation and equity from 1950 to 1990?
in_scope_units: Introduction to the condition of the economy after Independence and the decision to adopt planning.
The goals of Five Year Plans: growth, modernisation, self-reliance and equity.
Agriculture, land reforms and changes in ownership and tenancy.
The Green Revolution, food security, marketable surplus and the debate on subsidies.
Industry and trade, including public and private sectors and Industrial Policy Resolution 1956.
Trade policy, import substitution and protection of domestic industry.
Conclusion and appraisal of the 1950–1990 development strategy.
banned_topics: Colonial economic conditions before 1947, which belong to the previous chapter.
The 1991 balance-of-payments crisis and LPG reforms, which belong to the next chapter.
Detailed current agricultural-credit systems, which belong to Rural Development.

known_pitfalls.claim: Growth was the only goal of the Five Year Plans.
known_pitfalls.correction: The four major goals were growth, modernisation, self-reliance and equity.

known_pitfalls.claim: India adopted a purely socialist economy.
known_pitfalls.correction: India adopted a mixed economy with both public and private sectors.

known_pitfalls.claim: The Green Revolution benefited every crop and every region equally.
known_pitfalls.correction: It was initially concentrated in wheat and selected regions with irrigation and other inputs.

known_pitfalls.claim: Import substitution meant banning all international trade.
known_pitfalls.correction: It aimed to replace selected imports with domestic production through protection such as tariffs and quotas.

known_pitfalls.claim: Industrial licensing applied only to new public enterprises.
known_pitfalls.correction: Private firms required licences for new units, expansion and diversification.

recommended_example_progression: Use Exercise questions on the goals of Five Year Plans to distinguish growth, modernisation, self-reliance and equity.
Use the chapter’s land-reform discussion to analyse abolition of intermediaries and land ceilings.
Use the Green Revolution questions to compare food security gains with regional and class inequalities.
Use the IPR 1956 exercise to explain the public sector’s commanding-heights role.
Use the import-substitution exercise to assess protection of domestic industry.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with an EXERCISES section covering planning goals, agriculture, industrial policy, small-scale industry and import substitution, followed by Suggested Additional Activities.
